findings.title: Initial acknowledgment lacks a consistent deadline predicate
findings.rationale: The packet summary specifies explicit risk acknowledgment after the dispatch deadline, and the normative ordinary-admission contract enforces that condition. The initial-attempt contract instead permits acknowledgment for AMBIGUOUS or EXTERNAL_ACCEPTED_LOCAL_BLOCKED without identifying an applicable dispatch deadline or requiring it to have passed. A transport timeout can classify an initial attempt as AMBIGUOUS before its lease expires, so the endpoint description permits release while reconciliation would still treat the claim as live. Explicit duplicate-risk confirmation is already required, but the permitted release timing remains inconsistent.
findings.suggested_action: Identify the persisted deadline governing initial SENDING claims and freeze the acknowledgment predicate for SENDING-derived AMBIGUOUS attempts. State separately whether confirmed EXTERNAL_ACCEPTED_LOCAL_BLOCKED attempts may be acknowledged earlier. Reconcile the summary, endpoint table, state rules, DoD and validation cases. Test acknowledgment before and after the chosen deadline, successor admission and a late original result. If earlier initial acknowledgment is intentional, record that exception explicitly before approval.

findings.title: Cover first-inbound automation after manual conversation creation
findings.rationale: IncomingService passes acceptance.conversationCreated into the NOVA_CONVERSA trigger predicate. Manual open creates the conversation before any Message exists; consequently, the first later inbound message will have conversationCreated=false and will not activate that trigger, including when the operator opened the conversation and abandoned the initial send. This follows the inherited implementation, but the current consumer and validation matrices do not explicitly record this observable consequence of the new journey.
findings.suggested_action: Record the expected NOVA_CONVERSA behavior for a manually opened empty conversation and add a focused planned integration case covering open without send followed by the first inbound message. Assert that opening itself invokes no automation. Preserve the delivered trigger predicate unless a different product behavior is explicitly reviewed and admitted.
